necessary_context.content: F⊆R^n is a known convex feasible set; each round first selects x_t∈F and then receives a convex cost function c_t:F→R.
necessary_context.name: Online convex programming and information order

necessary_context.content: F is bounded, closed, and nonempty; every c_t is differentiable; a finite uniform gradient bound exists, with ||∇c_t(x)||₂≤N for every t and x∈F; an algorithm for computing the gradient is available; and P_F(y)=argmin_{x∈F}||x−y||₂ can be computed for every y∈R^n. Convexity follows from Definition 4.
necessary_context.name: Seven standing assumptions

necessary_context.content: R_A(T)=Σ_{t=1}^T c_t(x_t)−min_{u∈F}Σ_{t=1}^T c_t(u). D=diam₂(F). The source denotes the diameter and the gradient bound over all rounds by ||F|| and ||∇c||, respectively, and writes the latter as a maximum; standing assumption 5 provides a finite uniform upper bound. The record denotes this finite uniform upper bound by G and does not additionally claim that the gradient maximum is necessarily attained.
